key_insight: A physics-grounded digital twin combines weld-pool simulation, AI surrogates, and robot simulation to screen in-space welding conditions and control strategies before experimental testing.
engineering_relevance: Fast surrogate predictions could support adaptive robotic welding for on-orbit assembly and repair as travel speed changes.
method: Finite-volume thermal model includes phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and local pressure; gravity is assessed separately.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates predict weld responses.
Simulated UR5 controller adjusts the power-source setting near an L-shaped seam corner.
evidence_signal: The GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs in repeated five-fold cross-validation; finite-volume checks placed 12/12 closed-loop versus 9/12 open-loop points within an illustrative 1–3 mm root-side-width band.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based; thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and hardware-in-the-loop tests are needed to assess model and controller validity.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
